# Minimalist Blog

A same-origin blog application with registration, persistent inactivity-limited sessions, a searchable/sortable public feed, and author-only post management.

## Requirements

- Node.js 20 or newer and npm.
- SQLite is provided through the native `better-sqlite3` dependency; no external database service is needed.

## Run locally

1. Install dependencies with `npm install`.
2. Start the application with `npm start`.
3. Open `http://localhost:3000`.

The database is created automatically at `data/blog.sqlite`. Set `PORT` to change the listening port and `BLOG_DB_PATH` to choose another SQLite file. Keep the database file private and back it up using your normal operational process.

For development, `npm run dev` starts the same application with Node's file watcher. `npm run check` performs Node's built-in syntax checks. `npm test` runs the automated regression tests.

## Validation and behavior defaults

- Passwords must be 12–128 Unicode code points. They are stored as salted scrypt hashes; plaintext passwords are never persisted.
- Usernames must be 3–30 ASCII letters, digits, or underscores. Username and email identities are trimmed and lowercased before uniqueness checks. Emails are limited to 254 characters and checked for a basic valid address shape.
- Post titles are trimmed and limited to 1–120 characters; content is trimmed and limited to 1–10,000 characters. Search is live, case-insensitive substring matching in title or content, and limited to 100 characters.
- The default feed is creation date newest first. Explicit sort choices are title A–Z, title Z–A, modified newest first, and modified oldest first. Stable ties use creation time newest first, then post ID.
- Feed previews show up to 220 characters. Dates use the browser's local date/time format. Edited posts show an “Updated” date; unchanged posts show “Published.”
- Registration leads to Login, successful login leads Home, and logout returns to Login. A delete dialog can be cancelled without sending a delete request.
- Sessions are server-side SQLite records with an opaque HttpOnly cookie, SameSite=Strict, and a 30-minute sliding inactivity expiry. Set `NODE_ENV=production` when served over HTTPS to enable the Secure cookie flag. Configure `APP_ORIGIN` to the exact public origin (for example `https://blog.example.com`) when deployed behind a proxy; the server rejects state-changing requests from other origins and requires a same-origin custom request header.

## Security and deployment notes

The application uses parameterized database statements, server-side validation and post ownership checks, password hashing, rate limits on authentication endpoints, security response headers, and text-only post rendering. Never expose the app over plain HTTP in production. Set `APP_ORIGIN` and configure the reverse proxy to preserve the expected host/protocol; set `TRUST_PROXY=1` only when the app is actually behind a trusted proxy. Use a durable, access-controlled volume for the SQLite database.

The application intentionally does not provide image uploads, password reset/OTP, or rich-text editing.
